Although my favourite way to use an iPhone is naked and without a screen protector, on the iPhone 17 Pro I'm actually using both, and I'd recommend everyone give them a try. They're affordable enough that even if they don't last a full year, you won't feel the pinch.

Five years ago, Apple introduced Ceramic Shield glass to the iPhone display, claiming a fourfold improvement in drop protection and promising to reduce the incidence of cracked iPhone screens.

I've personally never cracked an iPhone screen, but after a year of use, there are always two or three deep scratches on the display.

This year's Ceramic Shield 2 front glass claims triple the scratch resistance.

Apple also says the front panel has improved anti-reflective properties this time, but compared to the nano-texture anti-reflective coating on the iPad Pro and MacBook Pro, the gap is still considerable.

Giving your iPhone 17 Pro screen a matte finish

For these reasons, I've been using a product I tried and liked a few years ago — Mothca's matte glass screen protector.

This product isn't perfect either. If I had my choice, I'd much prefer an iPhone with nano-texture that doesn't have slight rainbow effects and reduced brightness.

However, if you're interested in a matte screen, I'd still recommend giving it a try — especially since a single pack is only USD 9 and a double pack is USD 14, and the feel is better than what you'd expect at that price.

A slim protective case for when you need it

When it comes to iPhone cases, since I don't plan to use one every day, I don't want to spend too much.

I usually only put on a case before kayaking or mounting the iPhone on a motorbike handlebar. I'm also worried that the sharp edges of the protruding camera bump might scratch the orange aluminium surface.

I actually quite like black, but paired with cosmic orange it ends up looking too Halloween-ish — not suitable for year-round use. So I figured I'd pick a greyer colour to go with the orange, creating a kind of futuristic spacesuit feel.

I'm quite happy with a case I happened to stumble upon at a retail store a few days ago.

It's one from Spigen called the Thin Fit, available in black, gunmetal grey or dark green. I went with the grey, which matched the look I had in mind.

Spigen's retail price is USD 39.99, but the same one on Amazon is only USD 34.99.

I've noticed that many budget cases don't support MagSafe, which affects the performance of external batteries and magnetic mounts.

The Spigen Thin Fit does have MagSafe, and it even uses a capacitive Camera Control cover instead of just leaving a hole.

I like how this case wraps around the entire camera "ridge", because that's the spot I'm most concerned about in terms of durability.

Once fitted, it creates a really nice "orange circle" design that looks similar to the Digital Crown on the space black Apple Watch Ultra.

With cosmic orange, aside from the port at the bottom, the button covers also show through, achieving the orange accents on grey look I was after.

Another bonus is that once the case is on, you no longer see that orange aluminium edge around the screen. It looks fine on a naked phone, but if both the case and the screen are dark, and all you see in between is a thin orange edge, I find it really jarring.

Two budget iPhone 17 Pro accessory recommendations

The Mothca screen protector helps you avoid deep scratches, and if you like anti-reflective screens, its matte feel is genuinely excellent. The Spigen Thin Fit case has a metallic look and a smooth feel, without making the phone too bulky.
